e.meaning: tail; the closing passage of a piece of music
e.etymology: From the musical term coda, the passage that brings a piece to its close, from Italian coda, tail. As a name it also overlaps in sound with Koda and Cody.

assoc.t: coda, the closing section of a piece of music
CODA, the 2021 film that won Best Picture

e.etymology: A trimmed spelling of Harlow, an English place name and surname from Old English here, army, and hlaw, hill. Harlow gained glamour from 1930s film star Jean Harlow.
From Arabic aqsa, farthest, taken from al-Masjid al-Aqsa, the Farthest Mosque, in Jerusalem, one of the holiest sites in Islam. It is especially popular in Pakistan.
The English tree name, from Old English ac. The oak has long stood for strength and endurance, and the name follows Oakley into use for boys.
A spelling of Rain, the English weather word used as a name, made familiar by actor Rainn Wilson. In Estonia, Rain is separately a short form of Rainer.
namesakes: Rainn Wilson (actor who played Dwight Schrute on The Office)

e.etymology: In the US mostly a modern coinage in the pattern of Jared, Darren and Aaron. It also serves as an English spelling of the Hebrew name Yaron, he will sing.
The Portuguese form of Matthew, especially common in Brazil, from Greek Matthaios and Hebrew Mattityahu, gift of Yahweh.
A short form of names such as Kalvin, Kallan and Kaleb, and a K spelling of Cal. Kal-El is Superman's birth name in DC Comics.
namesakes: Kal Penn (actor in the Harold & Kumar films and House)

e.etymology: A spelling of Gretel used mostly by Spanish-speaking families. Gretel is a German pet form of Margarete, from Greek margarites, pearl, known from the Grimm tale Hansel and Gretel.

assoc.t: Gretel of the fairy tale Hansel and Gretel

e.etymology: A modern American coinage that puts a Z on the sound of Kayla and Layla, in the same family as Zayla and Zaylee.
A K spelling of the word culture, taken up after rappers Cardi B and Offset named their daughter Kulture in 2018, a nod to the Culture albums by Offset's group Migos.
namesakes: Kulture Kiari Cephus (daughter of Cardi B and Offset)

assoc.t: Kulture Cephus, daughter of Cardi B and Offset

e.etymology: From Irish Fionnán, a pet form of fionn, fair or blond. Saint Finan of Lindisfarne was a 7th-century Irish monk who led the church in Northumbria.

e.meaning: people of Ciar, the dark one
e.etymology: From County Kerry in Ireland, Irish Ciarraí, the people of Ciar, a name built on ciar, dark. It came into use as a first name in the 20th century, for girls first in Australia.
Usually taken as a variation of Devin with the sound of David and Gavin. Davin is also an Irish surname, from Ó Daimhín, descendant of the little stag.
The Spanish form of Latin Januarius, of January or devoted to Janus, the Roman god of doorways and beginnings. Saint Januarius, San Gennaro, is the patron saint of Naples.
A blend of the prefix Ja- and Kayla, coined in the United States in the 1990s.
The Spanish form of Patrick, from Latin Patricius, a patrician or nobleman. Saint Patrick, the 5th-century missionary to Ireland, is San Patricio in Spanish.

e.meaning: happiness; or from Gwynedd, a region of Wales
e.etymology: A spelling of Gwyneth, a Welsh name in use since the 1800s. It is probably a form of Gwynedd, the old kingdom of north Wales, and is often linked to Welsh gwynaeth, happiness.
namesakes: Gwyneth Paltrow (Oscar-winning actress and Goop founder, spelled Gwyneth)

e.etymology: The feminine of Aziz, from Arabic aziz, which means both dear or precious and mighty. Al-Aziz, the Almighty, is one of the names of God in Islam.
The Italian, German and Scandinavian form of Eleanor, which goes back to the Occitan name Aliénor borne by Eleanor of Aquitaine in the 1100s. Its original meaning is uncertain.
From Yiddish hinde, a hind or doe, one of the traditional Ashkenazi animal names alongside Hirsch and Ber. It is used today mainly in Hasidic communities.
An English surname for someone who lived by or kept a park, a nobleman's enclosed hunting ground. It has joined Brooks, Banks and Hayes among the s-ending surname names for boys.

assoc.t: Rosa Parks, civil rights icon (her surname)

e.etymology: From Greek exodos, a going out, from ex, out, and hodos, way. It is the title of the second book of the Bible, which tells of the Israelites leaving Egypt.

assoc.t: Exodus, the second book of the Bible
Exodus, Bob Marley's 1977 album and song

e.etymology: From the English combining form aero-, of the air or of flight, which comes from Greek aer, air. As a name it follows the sound of Arrow and Arlo.

assoc.t: Aero, short for clothing retailer Aéropostale

e.etymology: The Spanish short form of Javier, the name of Saint Francis Xavier's birthplace in Navarre, from Basque etxeberri, new house.
A respelling of Seven, the number long tied to luck and, in the Bible, to completeness. R&B singer Sevyn Streeter made the y spelling familiar.
A spelling of Lacey, a Norman surname brought to England by the de Lacy family, who came from Lassy in Calvados. It became a girls' name in the US in the 1970s.
The French form of Jacob and James, from Latin Iacobus, Greek Iakobos and Hebrew Ya'aqov. It was once so common in France that Jacques served as a generic name for a peasant.
namesakes: Jacques Pépin (French chef and television host)

e.etymology: The Portuguese spelling, and French without its accent, of Giselle, from the Germanic word gisil, pledge, the first part of many old compound names.
A spelling of Winifred, the English form of Welsh Gwenfrewi, the name of a 7th-century saint, reshaped by the Old English name Winfrith. The Welsh name begins with gwen, white or blessed.
namesakes: Winifred Sanderson (Bette Midler's witch in Hocus Pocus, spelled Winifred)

e.etymology: From Old English Osweald, os, god, and weald, power or rule. Saint Oswald was a 7th-century king of Northumbria.
namesakes: Oswald the Lucky Rabbit (Walt Disney's 1927 cartoon character)

assoc.t: Lee Harvey Oswald, assassin of President Kennedy
Oswald the Lucky Rabbit, early Disney cartoon star

e.note: Many Americans connect Oswald first with Lee Harvey Oswald, who shot President Kennedy.
